added_models.model: Somapacitan population PK/PD (IGF-I indirect-response) model from phase 1 data, simulating weekly doses in GH-deficient children

engagement.confidence_note: Full text (PMC6325982). Year is a proxy: the model supported REAL 3 dose selection, registered 2015-11-25; the paper was online 2018-04.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the model was run on phase 1 data before REAL 3 doses were chosen, so it is prospective.
engagement.quote: Furthermore, IGF-I levels are expected to be elevated from baseline throughout the dosing interval, indicating efficacy, while also remaining within the normal range less than +2 SDS, as is the case in multiple-dose trials in adults
engagement.note: Model simulated weekly somapacitan in GH-deficient children: IGF-I raised from baseline all week, below +2 SDS.
engagement.short: Simulated weekly IGF-I rise in children

engagement.magnitude_basis: average weekly IGF-I SDS rising from baseline with dose, below +2 SDS
engagement.confidence_note: Full text (PMC7069655). NCT02616562 results posted 2026-01-16; year from 2020 publication.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: REAL 3 cites the model and reuses it to derive IGF-I averages but does not restate the prior prediction.
engagement.quote: The mean (SD) of the model-derived IGF-I average SDS values over the week for somapacitan 0.04, 0.08, and 0.16 mg/kg/week were −1.62 (0.86), −1.09 (0.78), and 0.31 (1.06), respectively
engagement.note: In REAL 3 children, IGF-I SDS rose with dose and stayed below +2 SDS, as the model simulated.
engagement.reason: IGF-I rose in children as simulated

dose.confidence_note: Full text (PMC6325982). Year is a proxy: the model supported REAL 3 dose selection, registered 2015-11-25; the paper was online 2018-04.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the model was run on phase 1 data before REAL 3 doses were chosen, so it is prospective.
dose.quote: Based on the simulations, once-weekly dosing of 0.04 mg/kg/week is expected to provide peak IGF-I levels that match the average daily hGH treatment; 0.08 mg/kg/week is expected to provide average IGF-I levels that match the average daily hGH treatment
dose.note: Model predicted 0.08 mg/kg/week matches daily-GH average IGF-I, and 0.16 exceeds it without passing +2 SDS.
dose.short: 0.08 mg/kg/wk predicted to match daily GH

dose.magnitude_basis: weekly dose matching daily-GH average IGF-I SDS: predicted 0.08, observed about 0.12 mg/kg/week by interpolation (-1.09 at 0.08, 0.31 at 0.16, daily GH -0.40)
dose.confidence_note: Full text (PMC7069655). Interpolated matching dose is my arithmetic on reported group means; the model's own targets are stated.
dose.judgement: Paired by me. The 0.16 mg/kg/week target (above daily GH, below +2 SDS) held; the 0.08 'match' fell short by about 0.7 SDS, so partial.
dose.quote: Model-derived mean (SD) IGF-I SDS for the somapacitan groups was -1.62 (0.86), -1.09 (0.78), and 0.31 (1.06), respectively, vs -0.40 (1.50) observed for daily GH.
dose.note: 0.16 mg/kg/week gave IGF-I SDS 0.31 vs daily GH -0.40, below +2; 0.08 undershot daily GH.

added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkeys given Jintrolong (PEG-rhGH) 0.3-3 mg/kg/week for 52 weeks with up to 157-week recovery (choroid plexus vacuolation)

dose.confidence_note: Full text (PMC9336684). First-use year is a proxy: the GLP study cites 2017 CFDA GLP rules and ran ~4 years with recovery; Jintrolong was approved in China in 2014.
dose.judgement: Monkey study run after phase III/IV patient safety was known, so the track is a retrodiction.
dose.quote: The NOAEL was determined to be 3 mg/kg/week as the vacuolation in CP cells did not elicit structural changes and is not expected to have resulted in functional impairment in cynomolgus monkeys.
dose.note: Monkey NOAEL 3 mg/kg/week for PEG choroid plexus vacuolation, a >120-fold exposure margin over 0.2 mg/kg/week.

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL AUC margin >120.5x over pediatric 0.2 mg/kg/week; no excess adverse reactions in patients
dose.confidence_note: Full text (PMC9336684). Patient side is the sponsor's pooled phase III (n=360) and IV (n=3,000) safety; choroid plexus imaging was not done in children.
dose.judgement: Retro: monkeys were dosed after the clinical dose was known to be tolerated; reproduced it, so retro not same.
dose.quote: In clinical trials, Phase III (360 patients) and Phase IV (3,000 patients) studies with 26 weeks of treatment demonstrated no statistically significant difference in the incidence of ARs between the Jintrolong ® group and the daily rhGH injection control group.
dose.note: Children dosed at 0.2 mg/kg/week showed no excess adverse reactions versus daily rhGH, consistent with the monkey margin.
dose.short: Clinical dose tolerated as margin implied

safety.confidence_note: Full text (PMC9336684). First-use year is a proxy: the GLP study cites 2017 CFDA GLP rules and ran ~4 years with recovery; Jintrolong was approved in China in 2014.
safety.judgement: Monkey study run after phase III/IV patient safety was known, so the track is a retrodiction.
safety.quote: Furthermore, we previously predicted in the safety margin section that clinically no vacuolation and PEG accumulation would occur at a clinical dose of 0.2 mg/kg/week.
safety.note: Monkeys showed dose-dependent, partly reversible choroid plexus vacuolation without functional harm; none predicted at the clinical dose.
safety.short: CP vacuolation only far above clinical dose

safety.magnitude_basis: adverse-reaction incidence vs daily rhGH; no new adverse reactions
safety.confidence_note: Full text (PMC9336684). No vacuolation-specific measurement in patients; absence of new adverse reactions is the comparison.
safety.judgement: Retro: run after phase III/IV safety was known.
safety.quote: No new ARs, including those that would be associated with CP vacuolation, were observed in the Phase III clinical trial.
safety.note: Phase III and IV children showed no new adverse reactions, including any linked to choroid plexus vacuolation.
safety.reason: Monkey safety reproduced known human data

considered_not_added: Somapacitan PK/PD in adult GHD (BLA 761156 pharmacometrics, REAL 2 titration): adult GHD, not this tile's pediatric population
Somapacitan IGF-I monitoring linear models (Juul 2021, doi 10.1210/clinem/dgaa775): simulated-data tool, no comparison with patient outcomes found
Model-based somapacitan dosing in SGA/ISS/Noonan/Turner children (2026, doi 10.1210/jendso/bvag124): other indications, not GHD
Somavaratan PK/PD or in-silico dose model: none found; pediatric doses came from the phase 1b/2a IGF-I dose-finding
Pegpesen population PK/PD (2026) and other PEG-hGH preclinical papers (doi 10.2147/dddt.s517485): not class member drugs
Growth-response prediction models (KIGS/Ranke) and patient-derived cells, PDX, human challenge or genetic models: none applied to somapacitan, somatropin pegol or somavaratan
Healthy-volunteer IGF-I (Rasmussen 2014) and hypophysectomized-rat growth for somapacitan: same systems as existing draft tracks
